picks.excerpt: For the US 250th anniversary, the documentary "Declarations: Black Americans and the Revolutionary War" used generative AI to animate and voice historical subjects — premiering June 29 on PBS. The filmmakers argue the technology enables a form of historical representation previously impossible with traditional archival methods.

An AI technology company's contributions go uncredited on nearly 80% of the Hollywood projects it completes, as studios fear audience backlash even for legitimate uses that improve quality and workflow — not generative slop. The piece examines how AI's cosmetic secrecy is distorting the industry's public conversation.

Luca Guadagnino's film "Artificial" — which explores AI and human connection — is in talks with Neon for distribution after Amazon MGM decided it would be better served elsewhere, creating an unlikely irony: an AI-themed film losing its AI-forward studio. The story reflects Hollywood's deep ambivalence about AI-themed content.
